findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on IO errors (missing file, permission denied, truncated file)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file paths abort the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> and use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| IoError::ReadFailed { path: path.to_string(), source: e })

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric content or out-of-range values
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV lines abort the program instead of returning a typed parse error for the specific record
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> and use parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(|e| ParseError::Value { field: parts[0].clone(), source: e })

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs a lossy cast — values in [65536, u32::MAX] silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: numeric values that exceed u16::MAX are silently wrapped, corrupting data integrity with no error signal
findings.fix: parse directly as u16 (parse::<u16>()) or use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err() to reject out-of-range values

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a full Vec<String> just to index parts[0] and parts[1]; also parts[0] and parts[1] are unchecked indexing with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: malformed lines with fewer than 2 fields panic via index out of bounds; unnecessary heap allocation on every line
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::MalformedLine(line.clone())) to get name/value in one allocation-free step, then trim and parse each

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side effect inside what should be a pure parsing/transformation function
findings.failure_mode: I/O in the core makes the function non-deterministic, untestable in isolation, and couples parsing to console output
findings.fix: remove println! from load_frames; move logging into the imperative shell at the call site

findings.problem: load_frames returns Vec<Record> instead of Result<Vec<Record>, E>; all fallible operations (read, parse, indexing) silently panic
findings.failure_mode: every error path panics instead of propagating typed domain errors; callers have no way to handle recoverable failures
findings.fix: change signature to pub fn load_frames(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, FrameLoadError> where FrameLoadError is a typed enum covering IoError, MalformedLine, and ParseValue variants

findings.problem: .collect() into Vec<Record> has no try_reserve or capacity estimation for bounded input
findings.failure_mode: large files can trigger unhandled allocation failures; no bounded-allocation contract
findings.fix: estimate line count, call Vec::try_reserve(estimated) before the iterator chain, and handle AllocationError

findings.problem: no benchmarks, profiler data, or allocation evidence exist for load_frames
findings.failure_mode: no empirical basis to evaluate performance claims or hot-path behavior
findings.fix: add a criterion or custom micro-benchmark measuring throughput vs file size, with profiler allocation traces

findings.problem: no static-analysis evidence (cargo clippy with Holzman denials, Miri, etc.) documented
findings.failure_mode: potential issues remain undetected by tooling; no verification ledger
findings.fix: run cargo clippy --workspace --lib --bins --all-features -- -D warnings -D unsafe_code -D clippy::unwrap_used -D clippy::expect_used -D clippy::panic_in_result_fn -D clippy::indexing_slicing -D clippy::as_conversions and record exact output

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_frames throughput
no profiler data showing allocation profile per line
no Miri or Miri-compatible UB scan
no clippy run with Holzman-denial flags
